comparisons.peer_topic: New $25 billion common stock repurchase program authorization
comparisons.peer_summary: On July 24, 2024, the Board authorized a $25 billion common stock repurchase program effective August 1, 2024, replacing the previous program authorized in 2021, modified in 2023, and expired on August 1, 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America disclosed the authorization of new, significant multiyear share repurchase programs in 2024, replacing previous authorizations. Citi’s Board authorized a new $20 billion program in January 2025 (referencing 2024 activity) with $1.5 billion planned for Q1 2025, subject to regulatory uncertainty, whereas Bank of America’s Board authorized a $25 billion program effective August 1, 2024, explicitly replacing its previous program that expired on that date. Citi’s program is characterized by quarterly assessment due to regulatory capital requirements, while Bank of America’s new program was a clean replacement of a specific prior authorization.

sentences.text: • Citi returned $6.7 billion to common shareholders in the form of dividends ($4.2 billion) and share repurchases ($2.5 billion) in 2024. As previously disclosed, on January 13, 2025, Citigroup's Board of Directors authorized a new, multiyear $20 billion common stock repurchase program, with planned repurchases of $1.5 billion during the first quarter of 2025, subject to market conditions and other factors. After the first quarter of 2025, Citi will continue to assess the level of common share repurchases on a quarter-by-quarter basis given uncertainty regarding regulatory capital requirements, among other factors.

On July 24, 2024, the Board authorized a $25 billion common stock repurchase program, effective August 1, 2024, which replaced the Corporation's previous program that was initially authorized by the Board in 2021, modified in 2023 and expired on August 1, 2024.

comparisons.peer_topic: Capital Return and Regulatory Capital Ratios
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm returned $11.80 billion to shareholders via repurchases and dividends in 2024, while maintaining strong regulatory capital positions with a CET1 ratio of 15.0% under Standardized Rules and 15.3% under Advanced Rules as of December 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Goldman Sachs reported total capital returned to shareholders in 2024 via a mix of dividends and share repurchases, while simultaneously highlighting their regulatory capital strength. Citi returned $6.7 billion ($4.2B dividends, $2.5B repurchases) and noted uncertainty regarding regulatory capital requirements affecting future repurchases. In contrast, Goldman Sachs returned a larger absolute amount of $11.80 billion ($3.80B dividends, $8.00B repurchases) and cited maintaining strong CET1 ratios (15.0-15.3%) as part of its capital management philosophy, targeting a 50-100 basis point buffer above requirements.

During 2024, we returned a total of $11.80 billion of capital to common shareholders, including $8.00 billion of common share repurchases and $3.80 billion of common stock dividends.
As of December 2024, our CET1 capital ratio was 15.0% under the Standardized Capital Rules and 15.3% under the Advanced Capital Rules.

comparisons.peer_topic: New Common Share Repurchase Program Authorization
comparisons.peer_summary: On June 28, 2024, the Board authorized a new $30 billion common share repurchase program effective July 1, 2024, replacing the previous $30 billion program authorized in April 2022.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan Chase disclosed the authorization of new share repurchase programs in 2024/early 2025 that replaced prior authorizations. JPMorgan’s Board authorized a new $30 billion program effective July 1, 2024, replacing a $30 billion program from April 2022, allowing management discretion based on market conditions and capital position. Citi authorized a $20 billion program in January 2025, subject to quarterly assessment due to regulatory capital uncertainty. While both replaced prior caps, JPMorgan’s authorization was executed mid-year for the remainder of 2024, whereas Citi’s was announced early 2025 covering future quarters.
